notes: The flag was approved by Abkhazia's Supreme Council in 1992. Listed separately as a disputed/de facto entity; it is not a UN member state.

De facto Islamic Emirate white flag with Shahada; first adopted in 1997 and restored in 2021, with calligraphic variants. The former republic's 2013 tricolour remains used in some international and diplomatic settings; no universally accepted single current flag.

The red flag with black double-headed eagle became the independence flag on 28 November 1912. The communist star was removed in 1992; Law 8926 of 2002 standardised the eagle drawing. The eagle has older medieval antecedents, not a securely dated identical flag.
Exact creation year is disputed: accounts propose 1928, 1934, 1937 or a 1940s redesign. The FLN used the flag from 1954; national use began in 1962 and specifications were legislated in 1963.

Tricolour originated in 1866 and was formally recognised in 1942. The 1993 Constitution retained traditional symbols; a 1996 law required graphic standards, approved in 1999. The current-version year refers to this standard drawing, not creation of the tricolour.
Adopted at independence on 11 November 1975; reaffirmed by later constitutions.
Designed by Reginald Samuel in 1966; formally adopted 27 February 1967, before independence in 1981.
Belgrano created the blue-white flag in 1812; national adoption in 1816; sun added in 1818. Technical specifications were standardized in 2010.
Red-blue-orange tricolour originated in the First Republic; restored 24 August 1990 with different proportions. Flag law renewed in 2006.
Competition design first flown in 1901; stars revised in 1903 and Commonwealth Star changed to seven points in 1908; Flags Act 1953 took effect in 1954.

Red-white-red Babenberg banner is documented around 1230; this is not an exact creation date. Used as the republican flag from 1918, formally legislated in 1919 and restored in 1945. Entry refers to the plain national flag, not the eagle-bearing federal service flag.
Tricolour adopted 9 November 1918; restored nationally on 5 February 1991 after use in Nakhchivan from 1990.
National flag established at independence in 1973; Flags and Coat of Arms (Regulation) Act commenced 10 July 1973.
White strip added to red flag in 1820; serrations introduced in 1932. Present five-point serration adopted 14 February 2002.
Green field/red disc flag with a map was designed in June 1970 and first publicly hoisted in March 1971. Map removed in Kamrul Hasan's 1972 redesign.
Grantley Prescod's design was first raised at independence on 30 November 1966; becoming a republic in 2021 did not create a new national flag.

The red-green flag with ornamental hoist derives from the 1951 Byelorussian SSR flag. In 1995 Soviet emblems were removed and the ornament colours reversed. The ornamental pattern was modified in 2012.

Ducpetiaux and Jottrand designed the revolutionary flag on 26 August 1830 with horizontal stripes. The current vertical black-yellow-red arrangement dates to 1831; the 1789 Brabant revolutionary colours are an earlier precursor.

Origin refers to the unofficial blue flag with central arms presented in 1950; red top and bottom borders were added for the 1981 national flag. Current reproduction guidance published as 2025 guidelines.
Original Dahomey tricolour adopted in 1959; replaced in 1975 and restored in 1990.

First dragon flag made for the 1949 Indo-Bhutan Treaty. Rectangular format and white dragon developed in the 1950s; lower field changed to orange in 1968 or 1969, so no exact current-version year is asserted. National Flag Rules codified it in 1972.
Red-yellow-green horizontal tricolor established by law of 5 November 1851. This row dates the plain national tricolor; state versions add the coat of arms, whose drawing was standardized separately.
The High Representative established the current triangle-and-stars flag on 4 February 1998. Later legislation did not create this design.
The Botswana Emblems Act commenced at independence on 30 September 1966.
Origin refers to the imperial green field and yellow diamond of 1822. The republican celestial globe replaced the imperial arms in 1889; the current 27-star version dates to 1992.
Yellow-white-black design created in 1906; state crest added on 29 September 1959 and flag retained at independence in 1984.

Ivan Paraskevov's white-green-red Braila prototype, with a lion and swallowtail, was completed by his daughter Stiliyana in April 1877. The plain rectangular tricolour was legislated in 1879. The communist emblem was removed in 1990, restoring the plain design.
Adopted on 4 August 1984, replacing the Upper Volta flag; construction details were specified in 1997.
The saltire and central disc date to 1962; three stars replaced the former royal emblem in 1967. Proportions changed to 3:5 in 1982.
The 1992 constitutional revision introduced the current blue flag and circle of ten stars.
Current blue-red-blue Angkor Wat design first adopted in 1948; restored in 1993. Earlier temple flags had a different border arrangement. Sources differ on exact days, but agree on the years.
Vertical green-red-yellow tricolour dates to 1957; the present single central star was adopted in 1975.
Maple-leaf design developed and selected in 1964; royal proclamation signed in January 1965 and flag inaugurated 15 February 1965.
Adopted by the Legislative Assembly on 1 December 1958; attributed to Barthelemy Boganda.
Law 13 of 6 November 1959 established the blue-gold-red tricolour.
The Lone Star design was legalized on 18 October 1817; proportions were fixed in 1854 and star dimensions in 1912. Those specifications do not mark creation of a new flag pattern.
Zeng Liansong's five-star design was selected and adopted on 27 September 1949; first raised at the founding ceremony on 1 October.
Origin is Miranda's yellow-blue-red precursor, first flown in 1806; Colombia's current unequal-width national tricolor was officially adopted 26 November 1861.
The four-stripe design was prescribed by the constitution approved on 23 December 2001; earlier Comorian flags had different fields.

Origin refers to the fifteen-star ring on the 1973 green flag. The current blue ensign was adopted in 1979, with white stars and the Union Jack; a similar proposal had been submitted in the 1973 competition.

Five-stripe design established in 1848. Current_version_year refers to the official arms drawing used on the state flag/pabellon, set in 1998; the plain civil/national flag retains the 1848 stripe pattern. Use was codified again in 2022.
Law 59-240 of 3 December 1959 created the orange-white-green national emblem.
The red-white-blue tricolour dates to 1848. The present checkerboard arms and five-shield crown were introduced in December 1990.
Designed by Miguel Teurbe Tolon with Narciso Lopez in 1849; first flown in Cuba in 1850; adopted by the Republic in Arms in 1869 and by the independent republic in 1902.
Ismet Guney's map-and-olive-branches design won the 1960 competition and was first used on 16 August. Drawing, colours and proportions were standardized in 2006; this was not the design's creation.

Jaroslav Kurs's blue-wedge design was selected in 1919. The wedge was lengthened in January 1920 and the flag enacted on 30 March 1920 for Czechoslovakia. Czechia retained it when independent in 1993.
Sky-blue field with a yellow star and a yellow-edged red diagonal stripe introduced in 1963; the pattern was restored by the 2006 Constitution after intervening flags.

Exact creation and first adoption years are unknown. The 1219 origin is a legend commemorated officially. Secure evidence dates from the late 14th century, including the Gelre Armorial (approximately 1380); this is evidence of use, not creation.
The design is documented as a liberation-movement flag in 1972; adapted as the national flag on 27 June 1977. A separate exact creation year was not securely established.

Designed by Alwin Bully in 1978; cross stripes changed in 1981, parrot direction in 1988, and star edging in 1990. Government history highlights 1988; the 1990 detail is recorded by Flags of the World.
Duarte conceived the cross-and-quarters design in 1838; adopted nationally in 1844. The coat of arms used on the flag reached its standardized current form in 1913.
Origin is Miranda's shared tricolor precursor of 1806; adopted by Ecuador in 1830 and restored in 1860. The current national/state version with arms was fixed in 1900.
The red-white-black revolutionary tricolour dates to 1952; the current Eagle of Saladin version dates to 1984.

Origin refers to the blue-white-blue flag made for Manuel Jose Arce in 1822 and the subsequent Central American federation flag. El Salvador adopted the current national version with its own emblem in 1912.
Independence flag and tree arms introduced in 1968; the original arms were restored to the flag in 1979 after a 1973 replacement.
Triangular layout originated with the EPLF flag in 1977. Olive wreath replaced its star at independence in 1993; the current flag was officially standardized/adopted in 1995.
The first blue-black-white flag was consecrated on 4 June 1884; the colour combination had been chosen earlier. It became the state flag in 1918 and was restored in 1990.
Based on the regimental flag granted by King Sobhuza II in 1941; adapted and registered with the College of Arms in 1967. The national flag statute followed in 1968.

The rectangular tricolour family dates to 1897; early stripe order and emblems differed. The blue-disc yellow-pentagram version was introduced in 1996; a 2009 law replaced earlier legislation and refined specifications.
Origin refers to the colonial blue ensign with the 1908 arms. The present sky-blue flag, using the shield without supporters, was introduced at independence in 1970.

A blue-cross-on-white yacht-club flag with provincial arms was authorised in 1861. The national blue-cross flag was designed and legislated in 1918. This row refers to the plain national flag; state flags add arms.

Vertical tricolour naval precursor introduced in 1790 with red at the hoist. The current blue-white-red order dates to 15 February 1794; it was restored permanently in 1830. Later shade choices do not create a different basic design.
Green-yellow-blue arrangement introduced in 1959 with a French canton; the canton was removed and stripe widths adjusted in 1960.
Current red-blue-green design with white separators adopted at independence in 1965.
Five-cross flag associated with Georgia appears on Angelino Dulcert's 1339 portolan; this is documentary evidence, not a known creation date. Modern construction adopted on 14 January 2004.

Black-red-gold tricolours were used at the 1832 Hambach Festival; the colours became official in 1848 and were revived in 1919 and 1949. This row refers to the plain federal flag, not the federal service flag with shield.
Designed by Theodosia Okoh and adopted in 1957; the gold central stripe was restored in 1966 after an intervening white-stripe version.
The nine-stripe cross-canton design was adopted in 1822 as an ensign. In 1978 it became the sole national flag, replacing the separate plain-cross land flag.
Anthony C. George's design adopted at independence on 7 February 1974; an earlier separate design date was not established by the official source.
Vertical blue-white-blue national flag created by decree in 1871; colors and coat-of-arms details standardized in 1968.
Red-yellow-green vertical tricolour adopted on 10 November 1958.
The PAIGC adopted the basic design in 1961; the national flag adopted in 1973 omits the party initials.

Whitney Smith's own account dates his prototype submission to 1960; later accounts sometimes say 1961. Colors and borders were modified before the final design was approved by the House of Assembly in 1966.

Blue-red precursor created in 1803; bands turned horizontal in 1804 and republican arms added in 1806. After intervening flags, the blue-red flag was restored in 1986 and confirmed by the 1987 constitution.

Origin refers to the Central American blue-white-blue flag of 1823; Honduras added five stars in 1866. The 1949 decree specified the present four-corner-and-center star arrangement, proportions and turquoise shade. Renewed use of turquoise in 2022 enforced the existing color rule and did not create a new flag.

The red-white-green tricolour was used in the 1848 revolution. In 1957 the plain flag replaced the compulsory communist coat of arms. The colours are much older than the tricolour; the present Constitution retains the plain design.
Matthias Thordarson presented the design in 1906; approved in 1915, national at sovereignty in 1918, and retained under the 1944 republican flag law. The blue shade became darker in 1944.
Saffron-white-green tricolour with spinning wheel adopted by Congress in 1931, developing a 1921 proposal. Ashoka Chakra replaced spinning wheel in the national design adopted 22 July 1947.

Modern nationalist red-white flag documented at the 1928 Youth Congress; traditional red-white banners are older. Fatmawati sewed the surviving proclamation flag in 1944; national adoption and independence hoisting followed in 1945.

Green-white-red national colours with lion and sun were specified in the 1907 constitutional supplement; earlier tricolour variants existed. Current Islamic emblem and border inscriptions date to 1980.
Red-white-black three-star design adopted in 1963; inscription added in 1991 and restyled in 2004. Three stars removed in 2008.
The green-white-orange tricolour was first flown by Thomas Francis Meagher on 7 March 1848. Used by the Irish Free State from 1922; formally recognised in the 1937 Constitution.

Zionist movement flag used at the First Zionist Congress in 1897; national design and dimensions adopted on 28 October 1948. Similar earlier flags exist, so 1897 is a movement-adoption milestone, not an undisputed invention date.

The Cispadane Republic adopted green-white-red as a national tricolour on 7 January 1797, initially in a different arrangement. The plain republican vertical flag was established in June 1946 and confirmed by the Constitution effective in 1948.
Designed by a bipartisan House of Representatives committee and first raised at independence on 6 August 1962.

Sun-disc flag was used by ships by the 17th century; no securely established creation year. Naval and merchant versions officially specified in 1870. National status enacted in 1999; standard ratios and disc placement differ between the 1870 variants.
Royal and government accounts date the current star-bearing black-white-green flag to 1922; it was codified in the 1928 Basic Law. Arab Revolt banner of 1916 was its predecessor.
Shaken Niyazbekov's design selected in the 1992 competition; adopted 4 June 1992.
Present design adopted at independence on 12 December 1963; earlier KANU colours were adapted with white separators and a shield.

Flag introduced at independence in 1979 as a banner of the earlier coat of arms; the 1937 date belongs to the arms, not this national flag. Design subsequently codified in the National Identity Act 1989; the 1979 adoption date is from specialist history.
The blue flag with map and six stars was adopted at the declaration of independence on 17 February 2008. Kosovo has no officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; XK is a user-assigned convention.
New post-independence design prescribed by law on 7 September 1961 and amended that November.
Original sun-and-tunduk flag adopted 3 March 1992; rays changed from wavy to straight by the December 2023 law.
Maha Sila Viravong's design first adopted by Lao Issara in October 1945; restored for the Lao People's Democratic Republic in December 1975.

A red banner crossed by white is described for a Latvian military unit in 1279; this is a historical precursor, not a proven date of creation. Ansis Cirulis developed the modern flag in 1917; it was legislated in 1921 and restored on 27 February 1990.
Red-white-red cedar design drawn and signed by parliamentarians in November 1943; adopted constitutionally in December 1943.
Horizontal blue-white-green design with the black Basotho hat introduced in October 2006, replacing the diagonal 1987 design.
Eleven-stripe, single-star independence flag dates to 1847; manufacturing specifications and proportions were further regulated in 1961.
Independence tricolour with crescent and star introduced in 1951; restored under the 2011 Constitutional Declaration.
Blue-red colours first appear on a standard design in 1793; the exact creation of the modern horizontal bicolour is uncertain. The princely crown was added in 1937; the flag law was codified in 1982.

The commission approved equal yellow-green-red stripes on 19 April 1918. State-flag status was restored on 18 November 1988. The original 3:5 proportions were reinstated in 2004; this was not a new basic design.

Red-white-light-blue flags appeared in the 1840s; in 1845 the governor circulated a standard red-white-blue specimen. The national flag was defined by law in 1972; technical colour specifications followed in 1993.
Design introduced in October 1958 before independence in 1960. Sources differ on the exact October adoption day, not on the year.
Independence flag introduced in 1964; replaced in 2010 and restored in 2012.
Mohamed Hamzah's competition design selected in 1949 and revised/adopted for Malaya in 1950. Stripes and star points increased from 11 to 14 in 1963.
Red-bordered green field with crescent introduced at an uncertain date, commonly placed between 1926 and the 1930s. Present version created in 1965 by removing the black-white hoist band.
Green-gold-red tricolour originated with the Mali Federation in 1959; the black kanaga figure was removed under the law of 20 January 1961.

The white-red bicolour predates the current state, but no exact creation year is established here. The George Cross was awarded in 1942 and added during colonial rule; the present flag without its former blue panel was adopted at independence in 1964. The 1091 origin story is unproven.
Flag by Emlain Kabua introduced during self-government in 1979; Official Flag of the Marshall Islands Act 1979 gives the design and legal adoption.
Green flag with gold crescent and star introduced in 1959; red top and bottom bands added in 2017.
Four equal red-blue-yellow-green stripes first raised at independence on 12 March 1968.
Green-white-red vertical tricolor with central eagle ordered in November 1821. The present arms drawing and flag were adopted in 1968; the 1984 symbols law reaffirmed them.
Origin is the six-star blue flag of the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands introduced in 1962; the federation's four-star national version was adopted in 1978.

The present Moldovan tricolour was adopted on 27 April 1990 and its new arms added in November 1990. The 2010 flag law added the mirrored arms to the reverse. Blue-yellow-red has older Romanian/Moldavian antecedents; 1990 dates this state's flag.
The red-over-white national bicolour was prescribed by the Sovereign Ordinance of 4 April 1881. The Grimaldi colours are older; their medieval origin is not the creation date of this flag.
Red-blue-red Soyombo design created in 1945; socialist star removed in 1992. Colours standardized again in 2011.
The red field with gold border and gold double-headed eagle was established in 2004. Older Montenegrin military and royal flags supplied historical motifs but were not identical.
Dahir of 17 November 1915 added the green five-pointed star to the older red field. The plain red predecessor is not treated as the present design.

The horizontal FRELIMO-derived pattern was used as a transitional territorial flag in 1974-1975; the current emblem-bearing national version was adopted in 1983. The liberation-movement precursor is older.

Yellow-green-red tricolour with a peacock used in 1943-1945. Current white-star design specified in the 2008 constitution and introduced under the 2010 Union Flag Law; earlier tricolour is an antecedent, not the identical flag.
Unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 2 February 1990 and first raised at independence on 21 March 1990.
National flag first raised at independence on 31 January 1968; no earlier design-completion year was established.
Double-pennant flag predates the modern state specifications; no defensible single creation year. Current geometric construction and faceless sun/moon were adopted on 16 December 1962.

The first recorded Dutch tricolour in 1572 was orange-white-blue. Red gradually replaced orange during the 17th century; an exact creation year for the red-white-blue version is not established. Its colours were formally confirmed by royal decree in 1937.

Albert Hastings Markham designed the Southern Cross ensign in 1869 for government ships. The national flag was formally adopted in 1902; that year the gazetted specifications considerably enlarged the stars.

Origin refers to the Central American federation's blue-white-blue flag and triangular arms of 1823. Nicaragua's present national flag was definitively established in 1908; technical rules were codified in 1971.
Adopted on 23 November 1959, before independence in 1960.
Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi designed the flag in 1959; it was officially adopted and first raised at independence on 1 October 1960.
Current yellow ensign established by the Niue Flag Act 1975; self-government began in 1974, a different milestone.
New design trial-hoisted in July 1948 and formally introduced with the DPRK in September 1948.
The eight-ray sun flag was established by the law of 5 October 1995, replacing the 1992 sixteen-ray sun flag. The country's 2019 name change did not create a new flag.
Flag law adopted 7 March and published 9 March 1984 by the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, recognized as a state only by Turkey.
Fredrik Meltzer's design was chosen and approved in 1821. A union badge added in 1844 was removed from the civil flag by the 1898 Flag Act, effective in 1899; the original basic design was restored.
White-red-green design adopted 17 December 1970; emblem altered in 1985 and stripe/overall proportions changed in 1995. Royal Decree updated flag legislation in 2004.
Syed Amir-uddin Kedwaii's design was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 11 August 1947.
Blau Skebong's design won the 1979 competition. Public Law 7-6-2 approved the flag in October 1980; first officially hoisted on 1 January 1981, commonly listed as its adoption date.

Current stripe order was used by the late 1930s, but exact creation year is not established. Arab Revolt flag of 1916 is the ancestor. PLO specified/adopted this form in 1964; State of Palestine adopted it in 1988.
Designed by Manuel E. Amador in 1903; adopted provisionally by Law 64 of 1904, definitively by Law 4 of 1925, and ratified in 1941.
Susan Karike created the diagonal red-black design in 1971; adopted under the National Identity legislation that year, four years before independence.

flag_variant: National flag with different seals on the two faces
notes: Red-white-blue tricolor first raised in 1812; dual national seals established in 1842. Seal alterations made in 1970 were reversed by decree in 2013.

Vertical red-white-red layout introduced in May 1822; arms replaced the central sun in 1825, and the plain national flag without arms was established for general use in 1950. The distinct diagonal flag of 1820 is an earlier predecessor, not this layout. Law 32251 (2025) legally attributes the national flag to the 1825 law.

Flag of the 1898 revolution was legislatively adopted again in 1920; geometry standardized in 1936. Blue shade changed to royal blue by the 1998 Flag and Heraldic Code, without changing the basic composition.

The white-over-red bicolour and its proportions were established by the 1 August 1919 law. White and red had been formally adopted as national colours in 1831, but that measure concerned a cockade rather than a uniquely dated flag design. Later laws specified colour shades.
The commission developed the current design in October-November 1910; the government approved it on 29 November 1910. The Constituent Assembly formally legislated it in June 1911.

Nine-point maroon-white design with lettering and diamonds introduced in 1932. Lettering and diamonds removed in 1960, producing today's composition; 1971 marks independence, not creation. Technical law issued in 2012.
Approved in August 1959 and made official in September; replaced in 1969 and restored on 10 June 1991.

The revolutionary blue-yellow-red tricolour was adopted in 1848; the vertical arrangement was later established nationally. The current state flag without the communist arms dates to December 1989. Older plain civilian tricolours also existed.

A white-blue-red flag with an eagle is securely documented under Peter I in 1693; the 1668 Oryol design is less certain. The plain tricolour was restored in 1991; the 1993 decree fixed the current colour wording and 2:3 proportions. The 2000 law regulated its use.
Current blue-yellow-green flag with sun adopted in October 2001 and publicly launched in December 2001.
Designed by Edrice Lewis in the 1983 independence competition and adopted on 19 September 1983.

Dunstan St Omer's flag was introduced in 1967. Triangle proportions were revised at independence in 1979; the 2002 version mainly changed the blue shade. The official gazette dates the current approved flag to 22 February 2002. Earlier rendering specifications were not always implemented consistently.
Origin refers to the blue-yellow-green independence tricolor of 1979 with a different central emblem. Current three-diamond design adopted in October 1985.
Red flag with blue canton and Southern Cross introduced in 1948; fifth star added in 1949. Samoa's government dates formal adoption as the independent national flag to 1 January 1962.

The white-blue flag family is reported in use around 1797; this is not an exact proven creation date. Official adoption is conventionally dated to 1862. The arms and flag drawing were standardised by constitutional law in 2011.
Derived from the MLSTP flag adopted in 1972; the national version with a wider yellow stripe dates to 1975.
Present Shahada-and-sword arrangement approved on 11 March 1937. Earlier green religious banners are antecedents; 1973 is the flag law's year, not its creation.
Inherited the Mali Federation's 1959 green-gold-red tricolour; adopted the current central green star in 1960.

Serbian tricolours were established in 1835; the red-blue-white order followed the short-lived red-white-blue version that year. The present arms-bearing state flag was adopted in 2004 and its arms drawing standardised in 2010. A plain national flag is also official.
Designed by Philippe Uzice in a 1996 national competition; introduced in June 1996.
Green-white-blue tricolour first raised at independence on 27 April 1961.
Designed and adopted for the self-governing state in 1959; became the sovereign republic's national flag in 1965.

The white-blue-red tricolour dates to 1848. The current arms-bearing flag was introduced under the 1992 Constitution and first flown in September 1992; it became the independent state's flag on 1 January 1993.
Slovenian students first raised the white-blue-red national flag in Vienna in March 1848. The current flag with the new coat of arms was formalised on 24 June 1991.
Current design adopted 18 November 1977, before independence in July 1978; earlier 1975 competition designs were not the present flag.
Designed by Mohamed Awale Liban and adopted during the UN trusteeship in 1954; retained at independence and union in 1960.
Current green-white-red flag adopted on 14 October 1996. Somaliland is included separately as an additional entity with disputed sovereignty.
Brownell's initial convergence design was sketched on 25 August 1993; final colours and configuration were developed and adopted in 1994.
Taegeukgi documented in 1882 and proclaimed Korea's national flag in 1883. Republic of Korea construction standardized on 15 October 1949; later flag legislation did not create it.

The local foreign ministry dates revival of the white-red-yellow tricolour to 1989. State sources date the flag law to January 1992; other references cite a 1990 constitutional prescription and March 1992 regulation. Listed separately as a disputed/de facto entity.

Adopted for autonomous Southern Sudan in 2005 and retained by the independent state in 2011; derived from the SPLM flag. In 2023 authorities clarified sky blue and an upright star rather than announcing a new flag.

Charles III instituted the red-yellow-red naval flag on 28 May 1785. Its use expanded nationally in 1843. The current coat of arms was established in 1981; 1981 is not the origin of the red-yellow-red design.

Current overall composition with green and orange stripes approved by the design committee in 1950; parliamentary adoption followed in 1951. Lion flag was an older predecessor. Bo leaves revised in 1972; constitutional specification reaffirmed in 1978.
Current red-white-black flag with green hoist triangle adopted on 20 May 1970.
Current green-white-red flag with yellow star first raised at independence on 25 November 1975, replacing the different five-colored-star flag.

Blue-yellow cross banners are depicted in Johan III's ducal arms in 1557; a 1448 origin is conjectural. The 1906 flag law established the current form and colours following the end of the union with Norway.

The Swiss government dates creation of the current federal flag to 1840 and national adoption to 1848. The white-cross military emblem goes back to 1339; cross proportions were defined in 1889. A medieval emblem date is not the creation date of the modern national flag.

Green-white-black three-red-star design was specified in Article 4 of the 1930 constitution (often dated 1932 in flag summaries). Restored in December 2024 and written into the 13 March 2025 Constitutional Declaration; modern proportions differ.

flag_variant: Republic of China flag used in Taiwan
notes: Republic of China flag: red field added to the earlier blue-white sun flag in 1906. Used by the Guangzhou government from 1921; national law promulgated in 1928. ROC flag is used in Taiwan; sovereignty is disputed.
Red-white-green crown-and-seven-stars national flag adopted in November 1992.
Present design adopted on 30 June 1964 following the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.
Trairong red-white-blue design introduced by King Vajiravudh in 1917; older elephant flags are different designs.
First adopted at the independence proclamation on 28 November 1975; restored with independence on 20 May 2002.
Paul Ahyi's design was established by the law of 23 April 1960, effective on independence day, 27 April 1960.

Origin refers to the red-cross-on-white flag of 1862; this became the canton of the current red flag in 1866. The 1875 constitution protected the existing flag. Earlier-use dates are reported by specialist sources, not an independently retrieved 1862 decree.

The red-green-red flag with Soviet emblems derives from the Moldavian SSR flag of 1952. Transnistrian authorities approved it on 2 September 1991; a 2000 law standardised its use. Listed separately as a disputed/de facto entity.
Designed and selected by the Independence Committee in 1962; Cabinet approved the committee report in June, before independence in August.

Official commemorations date creation to 20 October 1827 and adoption to 1831, but historians also propose circa 1830 or 1835. Constitution reaffirmed it in 1959; detailed specifications date to 1999.
Ottoman red flag with white crescent and five-pointed star adopted in 1844; Turkish Republic standardized it by law in 1936, with a replacement flag law in 1983.
Original independent-state flag adopted 19 February 1992. Olive branches added in 1997; current construction/proportions date to the 2001 revision.
Nine-star light-blue ensign introduced at independence in 1978; replaced in 1995 and restored in 1997. Restoration is not a new creation date.
Current six-stripe flag with crested crane adopted at independence on 9 October 1962.

The blue-yellow national bicolour was raised in Lviv in 1848; state use followed during 1917-1921. The current independent state formally adopted it on 28 January 1992. Modern law sets the ratio at 2:3.
Abdullah Mohammed Al Ma'enah's competition design selected in 1971 and first hoisted on 2 December 1971.
The first Union Flag combined the English and Scottish crosses in 1606. The current design added St Patrick's cross and was established by royal proclamation on 1 January 1801.
Stars and Stripes authorized by Congress in 1777. The present 50-star arrangement took effect on 4 July 1960, following Executive Order 10834 of 1959.

Stripe-and-sun flag created in 1828; number of blue stripes reduced to four in 1830. Official education history dates the familiar alternating straight/wavy sun rays to 1930; detailed dimensions were codified in 1952.
Independent-state national flag adopted by law on 18 November 1991.
National symbols declared in 1980 with government rights effective from 18 February, before July independence. Source reproduces the contemporary official gazette.

The Vatican's official history identifies a yellow-white papal flag in 1824, initially diagonal; papal yellow-white colours date to 1808. The modern Vatican City flag dates to 1929. The Holy See is the UN observer; Vatican City is its territorial state.

flag_variant: National/state flag with stars and arms
notes: Miranda's yellow-blue-red tricolor first flown in 1806; current eight-star version and revised arms introduced in 2006.
Red flag with golden star first appeared in the 1940 uprising; adopted by the DRV in 1945. Star geometry revised in 1955; flag retained for reunified Vietnam in 1976.

SADR flag adopted on 27 February 1976; earlier Polisario use is reported but its exact design-creation date was not securely established. Territory is disputed and also claimed/administered in part by Morocco.
Plain red-white-black tricolour adopted for united Yemen on 22 May 1990; related North and South Yemeni flags previously carried distinct emblems.
Adopted at independence in 1964; the eagle drawing and green shade were modified in 1996.
The independence flag was designed and approved in March 1980 and introduced on 18 April 1980.
